problem: Evaluate the line integral of the function $f(x,y)=xy(3+2{y}^{2})$ along the ellipse $C$ with equation ${x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}=9,$ traversed once in the counterclockwise direction.
worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

Note that we can write the equation of our ellipse in the form

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}}=1.
$$

So, the curve $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $3$ and $\sqrt{3},$ respectively. Therefore, it can be parametrized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,0\le t\le 2\pi .
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡t+3{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{6{sin}^{2}⁡t+3({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{3+6{sin}^{2}⁡t}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=xy(3+2{y}^{2})$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (3+2(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2})=3\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,(3+6{sin}^{2}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}xy(3+2{y}^{2})\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }3\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t(3+6{sin}^{2}⁡t)\cdot \sqrt{3+6{sin}^{2}⁡t}\cdot \text{d}t \\  & =3\sqrt{3}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t{(3+6{sin}^{2}⁡t)}^{3/2}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=3+6{sin}^{2}⁡t,$ $\text{d}u=12\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\sqrt{3}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t{(3+6{sin}^{2}⁡t)}^{3/2}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}{\int }_{3}^{3}{u}^{3/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\cdot \frac{2}{5}{u}^{5/2}{|}_{3}^{3} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
